'''Sir Peter Leonard Knight''' {{postnom|country=GBR|FRS|HonFInstP}} (born 12 August 1947) is a British [[physicist]], professor of [[quantum optics]] and senior research investigator at [[Imperial College London]], and principal of the [[Royal Society#Kavli Royal Society International Centre|Kavli Royal Society International Centre]].<ref>{{Cite web|url-access=subscription|url=https://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/10.1093/ww/9780199540884.001.0001/ww-9780199540884-e-23334|title=Knight, Prof. Sir Peter Leonard, (born 12 Aug. 1947), Professor of Quantum Optics, 1988–2010, now Emeritus, Senior Principal, 2008–09, and Deputy Rector (Research), 2009–10, Imperial College of Science, Technology and Medicine; Senior Fellow in Residence (formerly Principal), Kavli Royal Society International Centre, Chicheley Hall, 2010–19|website=WHO'S WHO & WHO WAS WHO|doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U23334|isbn=978-0-19-954088-4}}</ref><ref name="icl2019">{{cite web |title=Emeritus Professor Sir Peter Knight |url=https://www.imperial.ac.uk/people/p.knight |website=Imperial College London |access-date=23 November 2019}}</ref> He is a leading academic in the field of quantum [[optics]], and the recipient of several major awards including the [[Royal Medal]] from the [[Royal Society]] and the [[Thomas Young Medal and Prize]] from the [[Institute of Physics]]. He is a former president of the [[Institute of Physics]] and [[Optica (society)|Optica]] (then Optical Society of America), the first non North American-based person to take the position.
He is described as "one of the UK’s most influential scientists and leaders of scientific policy" by his peers.<ref name="glas2019" />

==Academic career==

Knight's work is concerned principally with theoretical [[quantum optics]], strong field physics and especially quantum information science. He was educated at [[Bedford Modern School]].<ref>"School of the Black and Red-A History of Bedford Modern School" by Andrew Underwood (1981); reset and updated by Peter Boon, Paul Middleton and Richard Wildman (2010).</ref>

When Knight began his university education he attended [[Sussex University]] to read chemistry, but soon realised physics interested him more.<ref name="guar2019">{{cite web |last1=Eliza |first1=Anyangwe |title=Science research is not a tap you can turn on and off at will |url=https://www.theguardian.com/higher-education-network/blog/2012/mar/20/sir-peter-knight-interview |website=The Guardian |date=20 March 2012 |access-date=23 November 2019}}</ref> He received his first degree and D.Phil. from [[Sussex University]] and became research associate at the Department of Physics and Astronomy of the [[University of Rochester]] and at the Physics Department and [[SLAC]], [[Stanford University]] (US). He spent three years doing post-doctoral research in the US in the group of Joseph Eberly which gave him experience of working with "incredibly gifted people".<ref name="guar2019" /> He was then SRC research fellow at [[Sussex University]], and later visiting scientist at the [[Johns Hopkins University]], [[Baltimore]], Maryland, US.<ref name="icl2019"/>

He became Jubilee Research Fellow from 1976 to 1978 at [[Royal Holloway, University of London]], followed by an SERC Advanced Fellowship from 1978 to 1983, first at RHC from 1978 to 1979, transferring in 1979 to Imperial College. He has remained at Imperial College ever since (apart from very frequent visits to the US), first as a lecturer 1983–1987, then reader 1987–1988 and professor since 1988. In addition, until 2010 he acted as deputy [[Rector (academia)|rector]] of Imperial College, having responsibility for the college's research.<ref name="icl2019"/>

In his capacity as a leading figure in quantum optics, Knight works on several advisory boards, including the UK Quantum Technology Initiative Strategy Advisory Board, the Photonics EPSRC Innovative Manufacturing Centre, the Winton Programme for the Physics of Sustainability in Cambridge and for several year was Chair of the Defence Scientific Advisory Council at the Ministry of Defence.<ref name="npl2019" />

Knight has also spoken publicly about science funding in the UK, and cautioned against cuts or pauses in funding and its effect on the British economy<ref name="guar2019" /><ref name="Iopfund2019">{{cite web |title=Asking for a "strong, positive signal" for science |url=http://www.iop.org/news/11/oct/page_52403.html |website=Institute of Physics |access-date=23 November 2019}}</ref> and regularly advocates for girls in [[Science, technology, engineering, and mathematics|STEM]] subjects and women in science.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Collins |first1=Nick |title=Half of schools register no girls for physics A-levels |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/education/educationnews/9584932/Half-of-schools-register-no-girls-for-physics-A-level.html |website=The Daily Telegraph|location=London |access-date=23 November 2019|date=3 October 2012 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Day |first1=Elizabeth |title=Why don't more girls study physics? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/education/2012/dec/30/why-dont-girls-study-physics |website=The Observer |date=30 December 2012 |access-date=23 November 2019}}</ref>

In addition to his academic work Knight was editor for more than 20 years of ''[[Journal of Modern Optics]]'' and remains editor of ''[[Contemporary Physics]]''.<ref name="npl2019">{{cite web |title=Professor Sir Peter Knight FRS |url=https://www.npl.co.uk/people/peter-knight |website=National Physics Laboratory |access-date=23 November 2019}}</ref>

Knight is described by the [[Royal Society]] as "an influential figure within the wider UK physics community"<ref name="rs2019">{{cite web |title=Peter Knight Biography |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/peter-knight-11760/ |website=Royal Society |access-date=23 November 2019}}</ref> and by [[Miles J. Padgett]] of the University of Glasgow as "one of the UK’s most influential scientists and leaders of scientific policy."<ref name="glas2019" />

==Senior positions==
Knight is [[Emeritus]] Professor in the department of physics at [[Imperial College London]].<ref name="icl2019" /> From 1 October 2010, he was the principal and is now Senior Fellow in Residence of the Kavli Royal Society International Centre at [[Chicheley Hall]]. He has been a visiting professor at the University of Louvain-la-Neuve, a Humboldt Research Award holder at the University of Konstanz and a visiting scholar at the University of Texas at Austin and at the University of Rochester.<ref name="icl2019"/>

Since 1999 Knight has been a fellow of the [[Royal Society]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://royalsociety.org/people/peter-knight-11760/ | title=Sir Peter Knight FRS | website=royal society.org | access-date=23 November 2019}}</ref>

Knight was president of the [[Institute of Physics]] from 2011 to 2013; president in 2004 of [[Optica (society)|Optica]], the first non North American-based person to take the position;<ref name="iop2019">{{cite web |title=Professor Sir Peter Knight |url=https://www.iop.org/about/awards/hon_fellowship/hon_fellows/page_64159.html |website=Institute of Physics |access-date=23 November 2019}}</ref> and a fellow of the [[Royal Society]]. In addition he was a member of the council of the Royal Society. He has a seat on the European advisory board of [[Princeton University Press]].<ref>[http://press.princeton.edu/about_pup/european_advisory_board.html Sir Peter Knight profile] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110608160559/http://press.princeton.edu/about_pup/european_advisory_board.html |date=8 June 2011 }}, Princeton University Press, European Advisory Board; accessed 7 April 2016.</ref> He was elected an honorary fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]] in recognition of his "major contributions to physics through his pre-eminent research, his influential leadership roles and his service to the Institute of Physics".<ref name="iop2019" />

Knight was chief scientific advisor until his retirement to the [[National Physical Laboratory (United Kingdom)|National Physical Laboratory]], and is chair of NPL's Quantum Metrology Institute. He continues to act as an advisor to the British government.<ref name="iop2019" />

==Other awards==
Knight was knighted in the Queen's [[2005 Birthday Honours]].

He was the recipient of the [[Frederic Ives Medal]] in 2008,<ref>{{cite news|title=Past Presidents of the Optical Society of America|publisher=Optical Society of America|url=http://www.osa.org/aboutosa/leadership/pastpresidents/default.aspx}}</ref> and the [[Royal Medal]] in 2010.

He has received awards from the [[Institute of Physics]] including the [[Young Medal and Prize|Thomas Young Medal]] (1999) and the [[Richard Glazebrook Medal and Prize|Glazebrook Medal]].<ref name="npl2019" />

Knight has received many honorary doctorates including an honorary doctorate from [[Heriot-Watt University]] in 2010,<ref name="icl2019"/> from [[University of Sussex]] in 2010,<ref>{{cite web |title=Sussex's winter Graduation is a worldwide celebration |url=http://www.sussex.ac.uk/broadcast/read/3080 |website=University of Sussex |access-date=23 November 2019}}</ref> from [[University of Glasgow]] in 2015<ref name="glas2019">{{cite web |title=Commemoration Day |url=https://www.gla.ac.uk/media/Media_410046_smxx.pdf |website=University of Glasgow |access-date=23 November 2019}}</ref> and [[University of Birmingham]] in 2017.<ref>{{cite web |title=University of Birmingham awards honorary degrees |url=https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/news/latest/2017/12/awards-honorary-degrees.aspx |website=University of Birmingham |access-date=23 November 2019}}</ref>

In 2012 he became a member of the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]].<ref>{{cite web |title= Peter Knight |url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/sir-peter-knight/|publisher=German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina |access-date=26 May 2021}}</ref>

In 2019 he received the Herbert Walther Award for his outstanding contribution to quantum information science.<ref name="Award2019">{{cite web |last1=Jackson |first1=Caroline |title=Congratulations to Sir Peter Knight |url=https://www.imperial.ac.uk/news/189787/congratulations-sir-peter-knight/ |website=Imperial College London |date=11 January 2019 |access-date=23 November 2019}}</ref>

Also in 2019 Knight received the highest accolade from the [[Institution of Engineering and Technology]], the [[IET Faraday Medal|Faraday Medal]] for his 'outstanding contribution in the field of quantum engineering',<ref name="Faraday2019">{{cite web |title=Imperial Accolades |url=https://www.imperial.ac.uk/news/193586/imperial-accolades-news-from-college/ |website=Imperial College London |date=25 October 2019 |access-date=23 November 2019}}</ref> acknowledging that 'His pivotal role in conceiving, designing and delivering the National Quantum Technologies Programme has put the UK quantum science and engineering at the front of the global race to establish the second information revolution.'<ref name="Faraday2019" /><ref name="you2019">{{cite web |title=Quantum Optics, Sir Peter Knight and a Faraday Medal |url=https://youtube.com/watch?v=OfCgAnO9s1A |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211214/OfCgAnO9s1A |archive-date=2021-12-14 |url-status=live|website=Institution of Engineering and Technology on Youtube | date=30 October 2019 |access-date=23 November 2019}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

He was named an Optica Honorary Member in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sir Peter L. Knight honored for quantum optical physics {{!}} Optica |url=https://www.optica.org/about/newsroom/news_releases/2024/february/sir_peter_l_knight_honored_for_quantum_optical_physics/ |access-date=2024-02-13 |website=optica.org}}</ref>

==Notable publications==
Knight is the author of several books and hundreds of academic papers.<ref>{{cite web |title=Peter Knight, Imperial College |url=https://scholar.google.co.uk/citations?user=SirKcyMAAAAJ&hl=en |website=Google scholar |access-date=23 November 2019}}</ref> He is an [[Institute for Scientific Information#ISI Highly Cited|ISI Highly Cited]] author.<ref name="icl2019" /> His publications include,:

* ''Concepts of quantum optics'' (1983, 18 editions) 
* ''Squeezed light : special issue'' (1987) with Rodney Loudon in ''[[Journal of Modern Optics]]''
* ''The quantum-jump approach to dissipative dynamics in quantum optics'' (1998) with M.B. Plenio in ''[[Reviews of Modern Physics]]''
* ''Atomic physics with super-high intensity lasers'' (1997) with M. Protopapas and Christoph Keitel in ''[[Reports on Progress in Physics]]''
* ''Introductory quantum optics'' (2004, 27 editions) with Christopher C. Gerry
* ''Springer handbook of atomic, molecular, and optical physics'' (2006) with [[Stefan Scheel|S. Scheel]] (chapter)
* ''The Jaynes-Cummings Model'' (2007) with Bruce Shore in ''[[Journal of Modern Optics]]''
